skill.name: azure-deploy
skill.description: Deploy already prepared Azure applications using azd, Azure CLI, Bicep, or Terraform workflows. The skill checks deployment prerequisites, guides execution, handles common failures, and verifies live endpoints.
skill.summary: Deploy prepared Azure applications with prerequisite checks, recovery guidance, and post-deploy verification.
skill.author: microsoft

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are documentation false positives from Markdown formatting, relative links, Azure examples, and expected deployment checks. Confirmed risks remain for remote pipe-to-shell installation, unsafe eval of azd environment output, cloud command execution, SQL role-grant construction, and registry password fallback guidance. No prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Remote install script is piped directly to bash.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the pipe-to-shell installer with package-manager instructions or a downloaded script that users can inspect and verify.

remediation.issue: Some examples use eval on azd environment output.
remediation.suggestion: Use safe key-value parsing like the included shell scripts, and reject unexpected variable names before exporting values.

remediation.issue: SQL role grants interpolate environment-derived service names.
remediation.suggestion: Validate service names against Azure naming rules, escape SQL identifiers and literals, and grant only required roles.

remediation.issue: ACR troubleshooting includes password-based registry login.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer Azure AD login and document admin-password fallback only as a last resort with cleanup and log-safety warnings.

remediation.issue: Deployment commands can mutate cloud resources with active credentials.
remediation.suggestion: Keep subscription, location, validation-proof, and destructive-action confirmations mandatory before running deployment commands.

semantic_findings.title: Unsafe azd Environment Evaluation
semantic_findings.description: Several documentation examples load azd environment values with eval. A crafted azd value could be interpreted as shell syntax when users copy these commands.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The eval pattern is explicit and repeated. The input comes from deployment environment values, which are not guaranteed to be safe shell syntax.

semantic_findings.title: Unescaped SQL Role Grant Construction
semantic_findings.description: SQL grant scripts build CREATE USER and ALTER ROLE statements with service names read from environment values. Unescaped identifiers and string literals can cause SQL injection or unintended privilege grants.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The role grants are clear and include db_ddladmin. Azure service names are usually constrained, so impact depends on input control, but the construction is still unsafe.

semantic_findings.title: Registry Admin Credential Exposure Guidance

semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The password retrieval command is explicit and followed by a password-based login. The document prefers AAD login, but still presents the credential fallback.

high_findings.confidence_reasoning: The eval pattern is explicit and repeated. The input comes from deployment environment values, which are not guaranteed to be safe shell syntax.

high_findings.title: Unescaped SQL Role Grant Construction
high_findings.description: SQL grant scripts build CREATE USER and ALTER ROLE statements with service names read from environment values. Unescaped identifiers and string literals can cause SQL injection or unintended privilege grants.
high_findings.confidence_reasoning: The role grants are clear and include db_ddladmin. Azure service names are usually constrained, so impact depends on input control, but the construction is still unsafe.

high_findings.title: Registry Admin Credential Exposure Guidance
high_findings.description: Troubleshooting guidance retrieves an Azure Container Registry password and passes it to Docker login. This can expose registry credentials through shell state or command logging.
high_findings.confidence_reasoning: The password retrieval command is explicit and followed by a password-based login. The document prefers AAD login, but still presents the credential fallback.

content.value_statement: Azure deployments often fail when environment, identity, and verification steps are skipped. This skill guides prepared projects through Azure deployment, checks, recovery, and post-deploy validation.
actual_capabilities: Verifies that a prepared deployment plan exists and is marked validated.
Guides azd, Azure CLI, Bicep, and Terraform deployment flows.
Checks subscription, region, resource group, and environment setup before deployment.
Provides RBAC health checks for Container Apps and Azure Container Registry.
Supports SQL managed identity setup and Entity Framework migration guidance.
Verifies deployed endpoints and reports fully qualified HTTPS URLs.
limitations: Does not create new applications or generate initial infrastructure plans.
Requires Azure credentials and installed deployment tools in the user environment.
Can modify Azure resources and may create cloud costs when commands run.
Depends on permissions in the selected subscription and resource group.

use_cases.title: Ship a Prepared Web App
use_cases.description: Deploy an application that already has an Azure plan, infrastructure files, and validation proof.

use_cases.title: Recover a Failed Azure Deployment
use_cases.description: Diagnose common azd, Container Apps, ACR, SQL, and Terraform deployment failures.

use_cases.title: Validate Production Readiness
use_cases.description: Confirm RBAC propagation, managed identity access, endpoint health, and post-deployment tasks.

prompt_templates.prompt: Review the latest Azure deployment failure, identify the likely cause, and apply the matching recovery steps.

prompt_templates.prompt: Deploy the prepared Azure app, verify RBAC propagation, configure SQL managed identity access, and validate all HTTPS endpoints.

output: Confirms the deployment plan status and validation proof.
Asks the user to confirm subscription and region choices.
Runs the selected deployment workflow and reports verified HTTPS endpoints.

output_examples.input: The Container Apps deployment cannot pull the image.
output: Checks the app identity and ACR role assignment.
Waits for RBAC propagation when the role exists but is not visible.
Recommends a safe retry only after the AcrPull role is confirmed.

output_examples.input: Finish deployment for an app that uses Azure SQL.
output: Reviews managed identity and SQL Entra administrator prerequisites.
Guides database role assignment and migration steps.
Verifies application health and database connectivity after deployment.

best_practices: Run this skill only after preparation and validation are complete.
Confirm subscription, location, and destructive actions with the user before execution.
Use managed identity and least-privilege RBAC for deployed Azure services.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill to create a new application from scratch.
Do not run deployment commands before checking the validated deployment plan.
Do not delete resource groups or environments without explicit user confirmation.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it when the application is already prepared and validated for Azure deployment.

faq.question: Can it create a new app or infrastructure plan?
faq.answer: No. It expects existing project files, infrastructure files, and a validated deployment plan.

faq.question: Which deployment tools does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers azd, Azure CLI, Bicep, Terraform, CI/CD examples, and common verification steps.

faq.question: Does it require Azure credentials?
faq.answer: Yes. Commands use the active Azure identity and require permissions for the target subscription.

faq.question: Can it change production resources?
faq.answer: Yes. Deployment commands can create, update, or delete Azure resources when the workflow requires it.

faq.question: How does it reduce deployment mistakes?
faq.answer: It enforces prerequisite checks, user confirmations, RBAC verification, and endpoint validation.
